data.one_liner: Serialize and deserialize common Flutter UI data classes and widgets.
data.what_it_does: Provides extension methods and functions to serialize and deserialize common Flutter UI data classes like colors, gradients, geometry, and text styles. Serialization is handled through extension methods while deserialization uses parsing functions.
use_when: You need to serialize common Flutter UI classes like Color, EdgeInsets, or TextStyle to JSON
You need to deserialize UI data from JSON without writing custom parser functions
avoid_when: You need automatic code generation for complex custom data models
You need features outside of the predefined list of supported Flutter classes
strengths: Supports a wide range of common UI classes out of the box
Simple API using extension methods and standalone parsing functions
Works with both material and standalone widgets libraries
weaknesses: Some class parsing is limited or not fully supported yet
Relies on manual parsing functions instead of build-time code generation
